description: Code edits from the DoH (Abu Dhabi) Claims and Adjudication Rules V2025.1: E&M follow-up, venipuncture/injection bundling, screening duplicates, and medically unlikely edits. SEAL's hospital is in Dubai; these Abu Dhabi rules are applied to its fictional insurers as an assumption, labelled with their source.

rules.title: Established-patient visit within 7 days of the first visit
rules.insurerNeeds: A follow-up visit within one week (same patient, specialty and facility) is billed with an established-patient code at zero value.

source.title: DoH Claims and Adjudication Rules
source.section: 4.2.1.3 E & M Services Not Separately Reimbursable
source.quote: Established patient, office outpatient visit occurring within 7 days from the initial New/established patient, office or other outpatient visit. … shall be billed using E&M code of an established patient codes 99211 to 99215 at "0" value.

rules.notes: DoH gives no denial code; PRCE-006 (Consultation within free follow up period) is the closest listed code.

rules.title: Venipuncture billed when the lab is in-house
rules.insurerNeeds: Venipuncture is payable only when the sample is analysed at an external laboratory outside the facility or facility group.

source.title: DoH Claims and Adjudication Rules
source.quote: Payment for venipuncture is only permitted when the analysis of the sample drawn is performed at an external laboratory outside the healthcare facility or healthcare facility group.

rules.notes: No code given; PRCE-002 (included in the allowance for another service) chosen.

rules.title: Venipuncture or injection billed with IV-contrast imaging
rules.insurerNeeds: Venipuncture and injection are incidental to imaging that uses intravenous contrast.

source.title: DoH Claims and Adjudication Rules
source.quote: Neither an injection procedure (96372-96379) nor a venipuncture (36415) should be reported with any diagnostic procedure code that involves the use of an intravenous contrast medium … These are considered incidental to the primary procedure.

rules.notes: The list of contrast imaging codes is SEAL's selection of 'with contrast' CPT codes for its specialties.

rules.title: Same screening test repeated within 90 days
rules.insurerNeeds: The same screening test is not paid twice within 90 days.

source.title: DoH Claims and Adjudication Rules
source.quote: In case of duplication of tests between IFHAS and other screening programs under Thiqa within a period of 90 days, the cost of that test will be subject to recovery.

rules.notes: DoH states this for IFHAS vs other Thiqa screening programmes and handles it by recovery. SEAL generalises it to any screening encounter and uses DUPL-002 (payment already made for same/similar service within set time frame) as the plan's S8 requires. The prior-activity check also matches the same code.

rules.title: Units above the medically unlikely edit
rules.insurerNeeds: No more units on one date of service than the code's medically unlikely edit allows.

source.title: DoH Claims and Adjudication Rules
source.quote: Medically Unlikely Edit (MUE), defines the maximum units of service that can be provided to a single beneficiary on a single date of service for a given HCPCS or CPT code … CPT 44970 … has an MUE of 1

rules.notes: Only DoH's worked example is encoded. The full MUE table ships in the DoH Mandatory Tariff workbook (Tab MUE), not yet downloaded — see research/README.md open items. DoH also says insurers 'opt to utilize' MUEs by contract.
